title: Builder Enrollment and the Enrollment Fee — Bridgewell New Home Builder Warranties Terms for Builders
content:
These terms govern how a home enters Bridgewell's New Home Builder Warranties: who may enroll it, by when, what the builder is billed, and what follows from payment or non-payment of that fee.

## Clauses

**1. Who enrolls.** Only a builder registered with Bridgewell enrolls homes, giving the builder registration number on file with the program. This is judged from the company's records of the builder's registration, matched on the registration number given, before the enrollment is made.

**2. Enrollment window.** A home is enrolled only when the builder enrolls it no later than the program's enrollment window, a number of calendar days, after the sale closes, counting from the day after the closing date with the boundary day included. The clock starts from the closing of the sale, as shown by the closing date for that property address; day one is the day after the closing date, and an enrollment made on the last day of the window is in time.

**3. The fee.** The builder is billed the greater of two amounts: the program's minimum builder enrollment fee, and the program's fee rate for each 1,000 dollars of the final sale price on the closing statement — that is, the final sale price divided by 1,000 and multiplied by the rate — rounded to the cent. Both figures are those of the program the home is enrolled in. The fee is billed to the builder for the home when the home is enrolled. The homeowner pays nothing for the warranty.

**4. Payment.** The fee is due the program's payment period in calendar days after the enrollment date. On payment the warranty is confirmed retroactively from the closing date: it leaves enrollment pending and enters the workmanship period, or, for a structural-only warranty, the structural period.

**5. Non-payment.** An enrollment whose fee is unpaid after that is voided, the fee is credited in full, and claims filed while it was pending are closed not covered; the homeowner is told to take the matter up with the builder. The void date is recorded as the warranty's end date.

The builder's fee balance for a home is the enrollment fee the builder owes for it; a positive balance means the builder owes Bridgewell. The fee billed raises it; the builder's payments and any credit (on a voided enrollment, or for a fee billed in error) reduce it.

## Clause 2 at the boundary (hypothetical dates, 30-day window)

| Closing date | Day one of the window | Last day of the window | Enrolled on | In time |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 March | 2 March | 31 March | 31 March | Yes |
| 1 March | 2 March | 31 March | 1 April | No |
| 10 June | 11 June | 10 July | 10 July | Yes |
| 10 June | 11 June | 10 July | 11 July | No |

## Clause 3 worked through (hypothetical figures)

Take a program billed at 2.75 USD for each 1,000 dollars with a minimum of 450.00 USD.

- Final sale price 412600.00 dollars: 412600.00 divided by 1,000 is 412.60; multiplied by 2.75 gives 1134.65. The greater of 1134.65 and 450.00 is 1134.65, so the builder is billed 1134.65 USD.
- Final sale price 150000.00 dollars: 150000.00 divided by 1,000 is 150.00; multiplied by 2.75 gives 412.50. The greater of 412.50 and 450.00 is 450.00, so the builder is billed 450.00 USD.

## Outcomes of the fee

| What happens to the fee | Status of the warranty | Effect |
|---|---|---|
| Paid | Workmanship period (structural period for a structural-only warranty) | Coverage confirmed retroactively from the closing date |
| Unpaid after the payment period | Voided | Fee credited in full; claims filed while pending closed not covered; homeowner told to take the matter up with the builder |

**Hypothetical date for clause 4.** A home enrolled on 12 March under a 30-day payment period has its fee due on 11 April.
